title: Valid Arrangement of Pairs (Eulerian Trail)

monster.name: Domino Sovereign
monster.title: Chainer of Head-to-Tail Pairs
monster.defeatQuote: Consecutive arrangement where end of pair i equals start of pair i+1 formed!

description: You are given a 2D integer array `pairs` where `pairs[i] = [starti, endi]`. An arrangement of `pairs` is valid if `pairs[i][1] == pairs[i + 1][0]` for all `0 <= i < pairs.length - 1`. Return any valid arrangement of `pairs`.
solutionCode:
def validArrangement(pairs: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    from collections import defaultdict
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    out_deg = defaultdict(int)
    in_deg = defaultdict(int)
    for u, v in pairs:
        graph[u].append(v)
        out_deg[u] += 1
        in_deg[v] += 1
    start = pairs[0][0]
    for node in out_deg:
        if out_deg[node] - in_deg[node] == 1:
            start = node
            break
    trail = []
    def dfs(u):
        while graph[u]:
            v = graph[u].pop()
            dfs(v)
        trail.append(u)
    dfs(start)
    trail.reverse()
    return [[trail[i], trail[i + 1]] for i in range(len(trail) - 1)]
hints: Eulerian path algorithm (Hierholzer). Start at vertex with out_degree - in_degree == 1.
